coaching.title: Active Recovery Day
coaching.message: Calendar calls it: Week 3, peak-volume block, recovery day — a big week follows, so protect it. No hard efforts. If the legs want to move, keep it to an optional 20-30 min very easy jog or walk, fully conversational, and only if it leaves you fresher, not more tired. Then Strength Session 1: single-leg work, hips, core, and eccentric step-downs. Those eccentric step-downs are your down-payment on the 2,500m of quad-pounding Julian Alps descent — this is race-specific work disguised as a rest day.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Recovery day target is ~220g carbs — don't cut them just because you're not running long; carbs are what refill the tank for the big week ahead. Prioritize protein for repair: aim ~1.8-2g/kg spread across the day, 30-40g per meal, with some within an hour of the strength session. Lean into anti-inflammatory foods (berries, leafy greens, fatty fish, olive oil, turmeric). Vegas heat plus travel dehydrates you fast — front-load fluids and add sodium so tomorrow starts topped up.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: This is where the adaptation from the B2B block actually banks. Ten minutes of mobility on hips, ankles, and t-spine, plus foam roll quads, calves, and glutes — the same descent muscles the strength session hit. Legs up the wall for 5-10 min to flush the travel swelling. Sleep is the real session today: aim 8+ hours, and with the time-zone churn, guard a consistent wind-down.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 37 days out from Kranjska Gora. Taking the easy day when your training is going well is a discipline, not a concession — the athletes who blow up in the Alps are usually the ones who couldn't sit still five weeks out. Choosing recovery is choosing to arrive at the start line loaded, not cooked. Trust the plan, do the strength work, and let the big week land on fresh legs.
